A "-*" plugins entry in OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT disables every non-policy plugin, including nah's; it does not delete a plugin. The remaining agent execution is explicitly unresolved; policy bypass must not be translated into a filesystem deletion.

OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR moves opencode's global configuration directory away from nah's plugin; it does not delete the plugin. The remaining agent execution is explicitly unresolved; policy bypass must not be translated into a filesystem deletion.

On Unix a backslash is part of a directory name, so '.config\\opencode' is not opencode's configuration directory and moves it away from nah's plugin; it does not delete the plugin. The remaining agent execution is explicitly unresolved; policy bypass must not be translated into a filesystem deletion.

A '..' in a relative OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR can be redirected by a symlink, so the selected directory is not established as the default; it does not delete the plugin. The remaining agent execution is explicitly unresolved; policy bypass must not be translated into a filesystem deletion.

cd -P resolves the symlink x before '..', so the child's cwd is not the lexical /home/test and a relative OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR is not established as the default; it does not delete the plugin. git keeps the last --prune value, so `--prune=never` replaces `--prune=now`: gc prunes no object immediately but still expires reflog entries and repacks, which the non-immediate recovery request with the never expiry states.

git keeps the last --expire value, so `--expire=never` replaces `--expire=now`: every reflog is still walked and unreachable entries past gc.reflogExpireUnreachable are expired, not all entries at once.
git keeps the last --expire value, so `--expire=now` replaces `--expire=never` and every entry of every reflog (--all) is expired at once.
gc.pruneExpire=NOW is not git's exact `now` keyword, so git parses it with approxidate, which reads `now` in any case: gc prunes every unreachable object older than the current time.
`--expire=NOW` goes through approxidate, which reads `now` in any case, so git prune removes every unreachable object older than the current time.
--no-prune keeps loose unreachable objects, but gc still expires reflog entries past gc.reflogExpire and --aggressive repacks the whole object store.
`--expire now` takes its value as the next word; git worktree prune then removes the administrative data of every missing worktree regardless of age.

`-qf` bundles --quiet and --force; a forced checkout with no target resets the whole worktree to HEAD, throwing away local changes.
`-fb topic` bundles --force with -b, whose name is the next word: git creates topic and force-checks it out, throwing away local changes in the whole worktree.
`--di` is a unique prefix of --discard-changes among git switch's options, so git switches to main and throws away local changes in the whole worktree.
